sections.heading: PSARA License Application Status & Approval Process: What Happens After You Apply
paragraphs: So you've submitted your PSARA license application, including paying the fee, uploading the documents, and completing all the other formalities? Now what? Will you receive a confirmation over a call, message, or email? Or will you have to check for it yourself? Will you have to go to visit the department office?
All these are questions that security agency owners think through after submitting their PSARA license registration application. This is something that many don’t usually tell.
Most guides and articles online will be centered around how to apply for a PSARA license, but usually very little on what follow-up they have to go through.

We do get calls about this every week. "I applied three weeks ago; nothing has changed on the portal; is that normal?" Yes, most of the time, it is. So, here is the guide that will take you through all the things after you have submitted your application: approval timeline, how to check your PSARA license application status, etc.
Your application doesn't go straight to a police officer's desk for verification. There's a queue, and there's a process.
The Controlling Authority's office receives your application and logs it
Save the application or reference number you get; you'll need it constantly
An official does a first-pass check for completeness (are all documents attached, is the fee paid, and are forms filled correctly?)
If something's missing, your file gets flagged before it even moves forward

This first stage is where a surprising number of applications lose time. An unsigned affidavit. A blurry scanned document. A financial statement that doesn't match the format the state wants. Small stuff, but it stalls everything behind it.

If you're still preparing your documents or haven't applied yet, it's worth going back to our complete PSARA license guide to double-check eligibility and paperwork before you submit the application. It will save you the headache.
Once your application clears that first check, it moves through several distinct stages. Knowing these helps you understand exactly where your file is sitting and why.

For document verification, the officials check your MOA, AOA (for a company), partnership deed (wherever is applicable), affidavits, office address proof, and all the other supporting and required documents. They go through all the documentation to see if everything is consistent, accurate, and genuine, matching every detail.
This is the big one. Honestly, this single step causes more delays than everything else combined.
